package_info.package_versions: prior to 2.1.3 (as used by humanize-ms in the context described)
package_info.why_malicious: The ms package, as a dependency of humanize-ms, contains a Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDOS) vulnerability. This allows an attacker to send specially crafted input that causes catastrophic backtracking in the package's regular expression parsing, resulting in excessive CPU usage and denial of service for the Node.js application.

execution_context.file_location: node_modules/ms/index.js (called via humanize-ms in application code)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code parses user-supplied time strings using a vulnerable regular expression, which, when given crafted input (e.g., a very long string ending in 'minutea'), causes catastrophic backtracking, resulting in excessive CPU usage and denial of service.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The use of an inefficient regular expression on untrusted user input can be exploited to cause a denial of service by consuming all available CPU resources.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior would be to efficiently parse time strings without risk of catastrophic backtracking or resource exhaustion. The actual behavior allows untrusted input to trigger a ReDOS condition.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Parsing time strings from user input is legitimate, but should be done with safe, bounded regular expressions.
key_indicators: Use of complex regular expressions on user input
No input length or format validation before regex execution
Denial of service observed with crafted input

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a specially crafted HTTP request with a very long string ending in 'minutea' as a todo item.
attack_chain.leads_to: Triggers vulnerable code in ms package

attack_chain.action: Application code (via humanize-ms) passes the unvalidated user input to the ms package for parsing.
attack_chain.leads_to: Vulnerable regex in ms package is executed

attack_chain.action: The ms package executes a regular expression on the crafted input, causing catastrophic backtracking.
attack_chain.leads_to: CPU usage spikes, application becomes unresponsive (denial of service)

behavioral_signatures: Excessive CPU usage during parsing of user-supplied time strings
Application hangs or becomes unresponsive after receiving large or malformed time input
Regex execution on unbounded user input
file_indicators: References to ms or humanize-ms in package.json
network_indicators: Large HTTP POST requests to endpoints accepting time or todo input
Repeated requests with long numeric strings and non-standard time units
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for excessive CPU usage or application hangs following requests with unusually long or malformed time strings. Scan dependencies for vulnerable versions of ms and humanize-ms. Use static analysis to identify unbounded regex execution on user input. Set up alerts for input fields that accept time strings and validate input length and format before processing.
